meta.description: Ice fishing has officially begun in the Detroit Lakes area! On Friday, I recorded a consistent 6” on Big and Little Detroit. Today, Little DL is at 8¼”. It’s amazing how fast ice builds when it’s this cold. South Lida was 5½–6½” on Saturday, and it’s likely near 8” now. There are ice ridges at every Detroit Lake access, which may make getting on a bit tricky. Unfortunately, snow is piling up and forming hard-packed drifts up to 12” deep. title: Detroit Lakes Fishing & Ice Report (12/2/25)| Baxstar Fishing

meta.description: Lakes are freezing over, and it is happening fast, which is a good reason to be excited!  I have heard reports of people venturing out onto the ice, so I really want to stress the importance of patience. While there may be 3”–4” on parts of certain lakes, that does not account for inconsistencies in the ice. Please give it a few more days before you consider walking out on any area lake. The truth is, some lakes will have ice thick enough and consistent enough to safely walk on by this weekend.

meta.description: The minnow bite continues to pick up steam in the Detroit Lakes area, but it isn’t the only live bait catching fish right now. Leeches and crawlers continue to catch fish, too. We’re catching ‘eyes in 22’-25’ but you can find them anywhere from 20’-30’ on Pelican, Detroit, and Big Cormorant, to name a few lakes. As reported many times this Summer, the number one producing presentation on my boat has been a drop shot rig. If you are not familiar, I highly recommend you try it out. Bottom bouncers

The accesses on Little Detroit were in rough shape but they have been cleared recently.  If I had to say which is better, I'd give the edge to the access by J & K/Hub

title: Detroit Lakes Fishing Report (2/20/24)| Baxstar Fishing

meta.description: This fishing was most very good this past week. Crappies are still biting like crazy near green weeds in 8-12’, as are bass and northerns.  Walleyes are being caught in the same depths, but also in deeper water, from 20’-25’. Crappies and 'eyes have been most active at night.  Use fatheads and wax worms for the crappies and rainbow chubs for for pike and walleyes.  Finally, big suckers have been catching big bass!  Please be careful right now, and plan on walking onto the ice, wherever you go.

meta.description: Rising temperatures will eventually spell the end of the hardwater season in the Detroit Lakes area. Remember, soft or slushy conditions near shore is the first sign that you should call it quits for the season.  If you encounter main lake ice that is cloudy or slushy, you should consider exiting the lake immediately, and then call it quits!  For those still fishing, good luck and be careful! Ice fishing has been excellent the past week up on Lake of the Woods (LOW), and the ice is still solid.

Conditions are shifting with the weather, and fish are responding accordingly. Crappies and bass are sliding shallow on sunny days as water temps climb, making for some solid action up tight near any structure. When temps dip or clouds roll in, expect fish to back off into deeper water, holding along weed edges and transition

title: Detroit Lakes Fishing Report (6/11/23)| Baxstar Fishing

meta.description: For those who have been fishing in 20+ mph winds this past week, I salute you! I’ve been guiding on a variety of lakes in the area the past few days and here is what I’ve seen. We have been catching walleye in the cabbage in 8’ on a bobber and leech on calm days. On windy days, a jig and minnow have produced eyes in 8’-13’. Crappies are relating to the cabbage as well right now, both in it and outside of it. We have caught big largemouth bass in 8’-13’ on large spinner baits and huge 7” plastic

title: Detroit Lakes Fishing Report (7/9/25)| Baxstar Fishing

meta.description: Grab your rod and reel and get out to your favorite fishing spot–the fish are biting! Here's the scoop.The largemouth bass fishing on Detroit Lake has been incredible. For those with a boat, it’s a great time to get out of your comfort zone and fish mid-lake weed lines, as opposed to fishing shorelines. You’ll find them in 9-12’ and they are aggressive! Crappies and bluegill can be found a little shallower in 7-10’. Plastics, small minnows, and nightcrawlers are your best bet for these species.

title: Detroit Lakes Fishing Report & MORE (5/27/25)| Baxstar Fishing

meta.description: Since last Friday I have guided 6 groups on the water. We caught fish of all species, but we also saw a lot of fish through the clear water in multiple lakes. There is no better time to see muskies than right now.  They are everywhere!  Remember, you can't target them until the muskie season begins on June 1st.  Here are the takeaways from my fishing marathon this weekend: Walleyes are consistently hanging out in 8’-14’. If you troll through these areas you will likely see multiple pods scatter

title: Detroit Lakes Ice & Fishing Report (12/4/24)| Baxstar Fishing

meta.description: Ice fishing has officially begun in the Detroit Lakes area, and local anglers couldn’t be more excited! There is 6"-7" of ice on many lakes, including Detroit, Sallie, Munson, & Leaf, to name a few. Crappie & walleye are active starting around 5 pm. Look for green weeds with your camera and fish the outside edge of that weedline. I suggest also putting a tip up shallower, in those green weeds & keep the minnow above them.  Witt's Quality Bait has some nice rainbow chubs and wax worms right now,
